Seurat 4 / Seurat 5 compatibility

Source: SEURAT_COMPAT.md

rscprep now detects whether Seurat 4 or Seurat 5 is installed and adjusts on its own. This note records what changed, which functions it touches, and where the two versions actually behave differently.

Tested against Seurat 4.4.0 / SeuratObject 4.1.4 and Seurat 5.4.0 / SeuratObject 5.3.0. The full test suite passes under both (676 tests under 4, 682 under 5; the difference is tests that only apply to one version and skip under the other).

Summary

Function Code changed? Behaves differently between v4 and v5?
mergeSeurat() Yes Yes, the biggest difference. Seurat 5’s merge() splits layers by sample. mergeSeurat() now joins them by default. New argument joinLayers.
runCellCycle() Yes Yes. Raw-data detection was broken under Seurat 5 and is now fixed.
diagnoseQC() No Only through doCellCycle = TRUE, which calls runCellCycle().
seuratFrom10x() No Returns Assay5 objects under v5 and Assay under v4. Same counts, same metadata.
includeMetadata() No No
flagQC(), getOutlierSummary() No No; they only read and write metadata.
rawMatrixFrom10x() No No; it returns plain matrices, not Seurat objects.
plotBarcodeRanks() Yes, for DropletUtils, not Seurat See the separate DropletUtils section at the end.
theme_prepro(), scale_*_prepro(), prepro_pal() No No

How detection works

All version handling lives in one internal file, R/seurat_compat.R. No exported function branches on the version itself; each one calls these helpers.

Helper What it does
isSeuratV5() TRUE when SeuratObject 5.0.0 or later is installed. It reads SeuratObject’s version, not Seurat’s, because the classes and accessors live in SeuratObject.
seuratV5Fn(name) Fetches a SeuratObject-5-only function (Layers, LayerData, JoinLayers) at call time with getExportedValue(). That way the package still installs and passes R CMD check against SeuratObject 4, where those functions don’t exist.
getLayerValues(obj, layer, assay) Reads "counts", "data" or "scale.data" the right way for each version: GetAssayData(slot = ) on v4, LayerData() on v5. On v5 it also stitches split per-sample layers (data.Sample_A, data.Sample_B, …) back into one matrix, and returns NULL when the layer doesn’t exist.
joinAssayLayers(obj) Seurat 5 only: joins the split layers of every Assay5 assay. A no-op on Seurat 4, and for any classic Assay (which has no layers).

SeuratObject was added to Imports in DESCRIPTION, since the package now calls it directly. It was already installed in every case, as a dependency of Seurat.

The object can be a different class from the installed version: an object saved under Seurat 4 still loads under Seurat 5 as a classic Assay, not an Assay5. So joinAssayLayers() checks each assay’s class rather than relying on isSeuratV5() alone.

The three differences that matter

1. merge() returns a different shape (affects mergeSeurat())

This is the change most likely to affect downstream code.

Seurat 4 Seurat 5
merge() output One counts matrix covering every cell One layer per input: counts.Sample_A, counts.Sample_B, …
After NormalizeData() One data matrix data.Sample_A, data.Sample_B, …

Code that expects one counts matrix (GetAssayData(), obj[["RNA"]]$counts, anything that indexes the assay directly) gets a different object depending on which version made it. Seurat 5’s own integration workflow (IntegrateLayers()) needs the layers split; most other code needs them joined.

What changed in mergeSeurat():

  • New argument joinLayers = TRUE. Under Seurat 5 the merged object’s layers are joined, so you get one counts layer, the same shape Seurat 4 returns. Under Seurat 4 the argument does nothing.
  • To keep the layers split for IntegrateLayers(), call mergeSeurat(objList, joinLayers = FALSE).

Behaviour change for existing Seurat 5 users: before this change, mergeSeurat() under Seurat 5 returned split layers. It now returns them joined. Any Seurat 5 code that relied on the split, such as a call to IntegrateLayers() straight after merging, needs joinLayers = FALSE.

Bug fixed along the way: mergeSeurat() counted cells with vapply(objList, ncol, integer(1)). Under SeuratObject 5, ncol() returns a double, so mergeSeurat() errored on every Seurat 5 merge with values must be type 'integer', but FUN(X[[1]]) result is type 'double'. It now uses numeric(1), which accepts both.

New check, same message on both versions: mergeSeurat() now checks, before merging, that every object has an Ident metadata column, and errors with The following element(s) of '<arg>' have no Ident column: <names>. Previously a missing Ident slipped through to the post-merge check, where SeuratObject raised its own internal error. That error was worded differently by v4 and v5 and named neither the argument nor the sample.

2. Unnormalised objects have no data layer (affects runCellCycle())

Seurat 4 Seurat 5
data right after CreateSeuratObject() A copy of counts Doesn’t exist until NormalizeData() runs
Asking for it Returns the copy GetAssayData(layer = "data") returns an empty 0 × 0 matrix with a warning
GetAssayData(slot = "data") Works Error: slot is defunct in SeuratObject 5

runCellCycle() normalises raw data before scoring, because scoring assumes normalised values. It decides whether data is raw with the internal looksUnnormalised(), which checks whether the data values are all whole numbers.

What was broken under Seurat 5: looksUnnormalised() called GetAssayData(slot = "data"). Under SeuratObject 5 that errors. The error was caught and turned into NA (“can’t tell”), so raw data was never detected. runCellCycle() then skipped normalisation, scored raw counts, and usually failed inside Seurat::CellCycleScoring().

What changed: looksUnnormalised() now reads through getLayerValues():

  • v4: reads the data slot, which holds the counts copy, and checks for whole numbers as before.
  • v5: if there is no data layer at all, returns TRUE (definitely raw) without inspecting anything. If one exists, it checks for whole numbers as on v4.
  • v5, after a merge with split layers: reads across all the data.* layers.

The same fix applies to diagnoseQC(..., doCellCycle = TRUE), which calls runCellCycle().

Seurat::CellCycleScoring() itself was checked under Seurat 5 with split layers and works, so runCellCycle() does not need to join them first.

3. Addressing assay data: slot versus layer

SeuratObject 5 renamed slot = to layer = in GetAssayData() and SetAssayData(), and has since made slot defunct. Any code calling GetAssayData(obj, slot = ...) now errors under v5 rather than just warning. In the package, the only place that did this was looksUnnormalised() (above). It now goes through getLayerValues(). The two remaining slot = calls in the codebase sit inside the Seurat 4 branches of getLayerValues() and the test helper set_data_layer(), which is correct.

Functions checked and found version-neutral

These were not changed. Their output under v4 and v5 was compared directly, by rendering the vignettes against both versions on real 10x data during this work, and was identical apart from Seurat 5 printing an extra N layers present line when an object is shown.

  • seuratFrom10x(): CreateSeuratObject() builds a classic Assay under v4 and an Assay5 under v5. Counts, nCount_RNA, nFeature_RNA, orig.ident and Ident are identical. The vignette used to say the function “forces classic (v4-style) Seurat assay objects internally”; it never did, and that sentence was removed in an earlier change. The vignettes have since been reverted, so the sentence is back in vignettes/seuratFrom10x.Rmd and should be removed again.
  • diagnoseQC(): Seurat::PercentageFeatureSet() gives the same pctMito and pctRibo on joined and on split layers.
  • includeMetadata(), flagQC(), getOutlierSummary(): these read and write @meta.data and @misc only, which did not change between versions.

Tests

File What it covers
tests/testthat/test-seurat_compat.R (new) isSeuratV5(); getLayerValues() on counts, on a missing v5 data layer (NULL), and on split layers; joinAssayLayers() on both versions; mergeSeurat() with joinLayers = TRUE and FALSE; runCellCycle() normalising raw data. Tests for Seurat 5-only behaviour skip under Seurat 4, and vice versa.
tests/testthat/test-mergeSeurat.R The Ident test now expects the package’s own message rather than SeuratObject’s.
tests/testthat/test-runCellCycle.R GetAssayData(slot = ) calls replaced with getLayerValues(); SetAssayData(slot = ) replaced with the new fixture set_data_layer().
tests/testthat/test-seuratFrom10x-manifest.R vapply(..., integer(1)) changed to numeric(1).
tests/testthat/helper-fixtures.R make_empty_seurat() builds a classic Assay under either version (it writes @counts/@data directly, which an Assay5 doesn’t have). New set_data_layer() writes normalised data under either version.

To run the suite against Seurat 5 without touching your main library, install Seurat 5 into a separate library and put it first on the path:

lib5 <- "~/R-seurat5"
dir.create(lib5)
install.packages(c("SeuratObject", "Seurat"), lib = lib5)

.libPaths(c(lib5, .libPaths()))
devtools::test()

Known gaps

  • Mixed lists. A list that mixes classic-Assay objects (for example, one saved under Seurat 4) with Assay5 objects made under Seurat 5 has not been tested through mergeSeurat().
  • Vignettes. These were reverted to their state before the example data was added, so they predate this work:
    • vignettes/seuratFrom10x.Rmd has the incorrect “forces classic assay objects” sentence again.
    • vignettes/plotBarcodeRanks.Rmd recommends df and fit.bounds, which do nothing with DropletUtils 1.30 and later (see below).
    All vignettes are eval = FALSE, so none of this breaks the site build.
  • runCellCycle() tests that use real ortholog conversion skip when orthogene is not installed, so the non-human path has only been tested with the conversion mocked.

Separate: DropletUtils 1.30 (plotBarcodeRanks())

This is not a Seurat change, but it came up in the same work and follows the same pattern: the installed version is detected from what the function returns.

From DropletUtils 1.30, barcodeRanks() finds the knee by tracing the curve instead of fitting a smoothing spline. It no longer returns a fitted column, and its fit.bounds and df arguments are ignored. plotBarcodeRanks() read fitted unconditionally, so it failed with arguments imply differing number of rows: 20650, 0.

What changed in plotBarcodeRanks():

  • data$fitted is NA when DropletUtils returns no spline (1.30 and later), and holds the spline as before on older versions.
  • The fitted line is drawn only when there is a spline to draw; the rest of the figure is unchanged.
  • The help page has a new “DropletUtils versions” section:
DropletUtils How the knee is found Arguments that tune it Fitted line
before 1.28 smoothing spline, then derivatives fit.bounds, df yes
1.28 spline; knee is the point farthest from the plateau-to-inflection line fit.bounds, df yes
1.30 and later curve tracing, no spline window, gradient.threshold no

The same data can give a different knee, and sometimes a different inflection, under different DropletUtils versions. Record packageVersion("DropletUtils") alongside any cutoff you report.

Tests in tests/testthat/test-plotBarcodeRanks.R hand summariseBarcodeRanks() both shapes of result directly, so both are covered whichever DropletUtils is installed.
